hypothesis: The exact v51 SOL Range-Onset route may retain after-cost edge under its native opposite-intent, 80-bps stop, and 48-hour fallback exits; its first attributable lifecycle must resolve before exit changes are justified.
decision: Continue the protected first v51 SOL long unchanged. Its current profit is below every predeclared completed-bar profit-lock activation and below the separately researched 60-bps fixed target, so the open mark does not justify an intervention or new live exit.
falsifier: Reject the implementation claim on any unexplained signal/route mismatch, missing protection, or exit-plan deviation. Weaken the edge claim if predeclared route-matched forward lifecycles become negative after exact costs or remain winner-concentrated. Reconsider native exits only if a frozen challenger improves chronological and side-separated results after costs and largest-winner removal.

findings.entry_contract: Fresh completed hourly SMA10/30 long cross with completed 5-minute RANGE admission; exact taker entry had zero measured slippage.
findings.native_exit_contract: Opposite selected executable intent, 80-bps fixed protective stop, or 48-hour maximum hold; no target and no live profit lock.
findings.current_exit_state: No opposite exit signal, target, or profit-lock activation has occurred. The venue stop is present and the maximum-hold deadline is not expired.
findings.challenger_context: The 60-bps fixed-target historical diagnostic was pooled-positive and positive excluding its largest winner, but only two of four blocks were positive and the benefit was entirely long-side; native remains the frozen control.
findings.interpretation: The current approximately 25-bps peak excursion is an informative first live path, not evidence that native exits are defective. Closing or locking it now would contaminate the predeclared live control.

limitations: The lifecycle remains open; its final PnL, exit reason, fees, funding, slippage, and giveback are unknown.
Completed one-minute candles approximate excursions and are not executable fills.
Estimated exit-now economics omit additional slippage and future funding.
The fixed-target surface was selected after prior live giveback and is not an untouched holdout.
One long lifecycle cannot establish bidirectional edge or optimal exits.
This record has no authority to close, resize, route, or modify the position.

recommendation.Recommendation: Preserve the exact SOL Range-Onset lifecycle and native exit control while recording its final outcome and the already-predeclared exit challengers report-only.
recommendation.Why now: The first attributable v51 SOL entry has occurred and is modestly profitable, creating a temptation to intervene before any challenger activation or resolved result.
recommendation.Evidence reviewed: Exact v51 entry and protection, frozen open-lifecycle audit, completed-candle MFE/MAE, current mark and costs, predeclared profit-lock states, fixed-target historical audit, and route configuration.
recommendation.Observed problem or opportunity: Open profit can return to the loss stop because native Range-Onset has no fixed target or profit lock, but the present peak has not crossed even the lowest predeclared 25-bps lock activation.
recommendation.Applicable market regime: Completed-hour long crossover admitted by a completed five-minute RANGE state, with the current context still structurally long and not emitting an opposite onset.
recommendation.Alternatives considered: Close immediately, add a live 25-bps profit lock, add the post-hoc 60-bps long target, shorten the 48-hour hold, or keep native exits as the forward control.
recommendation.Expected upside: Preserves unbiased evidence for a sparse mechanism whose historical returns depend on allowing some winners to develop.
recommendation.Main risks and failure modes: The open profit may reverse; a rare-winner mechanism may remain concentrated; the 48-hour fallback may incur opportunity cost; one side may lack edge.
recommendation.Validation completed: Exact entry/plan/stop identity, no ignored exit signal, completed-candle path completeness, current cost accounting, and historical target sensitivity with block and side decomposition.
recommendation.Validation still required: Resolved final exit and after-cost result, opposite-intent behavior, long and short forward samples, largest-winner sensitivity, and prospective comparison against frozen challenger policies.
recommendation.Success metrics: Correct protected lifecycle resolution, positive exact after-cost route economics, profit factor above one by side and pooled, positive net excluding the largest winner, and a challenger improvement that is stable across time blocks if any exit change is proposed.
recommendation.Failure / rollback triggers: Unprotected exposure or exit-plan mismatch is an incident; repeated route-matched negative closes or robust challenger superiority triggers a new approval-ready exit proposal.
recommendation.Confidence level: High for current implementation/protection; medium for preserving the control; low for durable profitability and optimal exit design.

single_highest_value_next_investigation: Resolve this first v51 SOL lifecycle and compare its native exit with the frozen 25/40/60-bps completed-bar locks and 60-bps fixed-target challenger using exact realized costs.
